run_note: Independent scheduled evergreen run. Reviewed all merged Tools & Guides guides and the 2026-10-21 ledger, checked current open PRs and confirmed #189 merged. Selected a new, self-contained application approval-boundary tutorial distinct from existing agent-environment permission comparisons. Python execution and production approval integration unavailable; article remains draft. No reviewed WebP cover or provenance yet.

candidates.title: Give AI Agents a Real Approval Boundary Before They Call Tools
candidates.reader_outcome: Implement and test a narrow Python gate that validates proposed tool calls and binds one-time approval to a requester and exact action.
candidates.reason: Existing ADE/agent comparison guides explain product-level permissions but do not teach a self-contained application-enforced approval boundary. Primary tool-use and OWASP guidance support the architecture. Distinct from RAG deployment and retrieval evaluation.

candidates.title: Deploying Your First RAG Application
candidates.reader_outcome: Run a local RAG API with FastAPI and Ollama.
candidates.reason: Already published in main and merged from PR #189; not a new learning outcome.

candidates.title: Evaluate RAG Retrieval Quality with a Golden Question Set
candidates.reader_outcome: Measure Recall@k and MRR@k with a labeled retrieval set.
candidates.reason: Already published in main and selected in the merged 2026-10-21 evergreen ledger.

candidates.title: Comparing Agentic Development Environments: Follow the Permissions
candidates.reader_outcome: Compare documented execution and permission controls across agentic development tools.
candidates.reason: Already published in main; a separate tutorial implementing an application-side gate is more useful than another comparison.

candidates.title: Checking whether generated RAG claims are supported
candidates.reader_outcome: Evaluate claim-to-passage support rather than only retrieval rank.
candidates.reason: Still requires a defensible labeled support-judgment set and protocol; avoid confusing reference presence with factual support.
